'''''Caulerpa prolifera''''' is a [[species]] of green alga, a [[seaweed]] in the family [[Caulerpaceae]]. It is the [[type species]] of the genus ''[[Caulerpa]]'', the [[type locality (biology)|type location]] being [[Alexandria]], [[Egypt]].<ref name=AlgaeBase>[http://www.algaebase.org/search/species/detail/?species_id=355 AlgaeBase] Retrieved August 18, 2011.</ref> It grows rapidly and forms a dense mass of vegetation on shallow sandy areas of the sea.

==Description==
[[File:Caulerpa prolifera.JPG|thumb|left|200px|''Caulerpa prolifera'']]
A plant of ''C. prolifera'' consists of a number of blades or laminae linked by underground [[stolon]]s which are fixed to the sandy [[Substrate (biology)|substrate]] by [[rhizoid]]s.<ref>[http://www.cavehill.uwi.edu/fpas/bcs/bl14apl/algae2.htm Morphological Diversity within the Algae] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110927004354/http://www.cavehill.uwi.edu/fpas/bcs/bl14apl/algae2.htm |date=2011-09-27 }} Retrieved August 18, 2011.</ref> The blades contain chlorophyll for [[photosynthesis]] though the green colour is somewhat masked by other pigments. Like other members of the order [[Bryopsidales]], each ''C. prolifera'' plant is an individual organism consisting of a giant single cell with multiple [[Nucleus (cell)|nuclei]]. [[Chloroplast]]s are free to move from one part of the organism to another as a response to the level of light at any point and there is a network of fibrous proteins that facilitates movement of [[organelle]]s.<ref name=CB>[https://www.angelfire.com/ri/skibizniz/bryopsidales.html The Cell Biology of the Bryopsidales] Retrieved August 18, 2011.</ref> Even when derived from the same source, individual plants of ''C. prolifera'' show great variability of form and it has been shown that this is in part related to the level of light. In bright locations, plants are compact, highly branched and dense, while in shady locations, populations typically have blades that are longer and thinner and can more efficiently make use of the limited light available.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Collado-Vides |first=L. |date=2002-04-10 |title=Morphological Plasticity of Caulerpa prolifera (Caulerpales, Chlorophyta) in Relation to Growth Form in a Coral Reef Lagoon |url=https://www.degruyter.com/document/doi/10.1515/BOT.2002.013/html |journal=Botanica Marina |language=en |volume=45 |issue=2 |pages=123–129 |doi=10.1515/BOT.2002.013|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Two distinct forms of the alga are recognised, ''Caulerpa prolifera f. obovata'' (J.Agardh) and ''Caulerpa prolifera f. zosterifolia'' (Børgesen).<ref name=WoRMS/>

==Distribution==
''C. prolifera'' occurs in shallow European waters, the Mediterranean Sea and the warm eastern Atlantic Ocean and also the eastern seaboard of the United States, Mexico and Brazil, as well as certain other scattered locations.<ref name=AlgaeBase/>

==Biology==
''Caulerpa'' spp. help consolidate the seabed and enable [[seagrass]]es to colonize the area. ''C. prolifera'' grows rapidly with growth taking place at night at the tips of blades and stolons. At dawn, the new tips are white, but during the day chloroplasts move into the newly available space. If parts of the plant become covered in sediment, chloroplasts can be withdrawn and moved to more productive parts.<ref>[https://www.jstor.org/pss/2440388 Cytoplasmic organization and rhythmic streaming in growing blades of ''Caulerpa prolifera''] Retrieved August 18, 2011.</ref>

Under normal conditions, [[asexual reproduction]] occurs by fragmentation. Pieces of tissue only a few millimetres across are capable of growing into new seaweed.<ref>Ceccherelli, G., L. Piazzi., 2001. Dispersal of ''Caulerpa racemosa'' fragments in the Mediterranean: lack of detachment time effect on Establishment. Bot. Mar. 44, 209-213.</ref>

Less usually, ''C. prolifera'' may undergo sexual reproduction by [[holocarpy]]. This may occur under conditions of stress with the entire cytoplasm undergoing [[gametogenesis]] and the original organism being left as a husk.<ref name=CB/> Such conditions occurred in 2005 after the passage of [[Hurricane Wilma]] over a lagoon in the [[Caribbean Sea]]. On that occasion, there was a synchronous spawning of ''C. prolifera'' and many other [[Bryopsidales|siphonous green algae]]. Besides turbulent water movement, the hurricane caused the sea temperature to drop from 29 to 19 °C in a few hours. This thermal anomaly seems to have triggered the mass spawning.<ref>[http://plosjournal.deepdyve.com/lp/de-gruyter/unusual-synchronous-spawning-by-green-algae-bryopsidales-after-the-bKs0Z0BbVT Unusual synchronous spawning by green algae (Bryopsidales), after the passage of Hurricane Wilma (2005)] Retrieved August 20, 2011.</ref>
